d: Representing relationships between entities. BFS finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs. DFS is for exhaustive search.

p: Graphs are represented using Adjacency Lists (HashMap of Node -> List of Neighbors). BFS (Queue) explores outwards in rings, perfect for Shortest Path. DFS (Stack/Recursion) explores deep into dead ends, perfect for connected components.
1. Build the adjacency list from edges.
2. Initialize a `visited` set to prevent infinite loops.
3. BFS: Use a deque, popleft, add neighbors.
4. DFS: Recursive call on all unvisited neighbors.

def dfs(node, adj, visited):
  if node in visited: return
  visited.add(node)
  print(node)
  for neighbor in adj[node]:
    dfs(neighbor, adj, visited)
Time: O(V + E) where V is vertices, E is edges. Space: O(V + E).

Adjacency List:      Adjacency Matrix:
A -> [B, C]          A  B  C
B -> [A, C]        A[0  1  1]
C -> [A, B]        B[1  0  1]
                   C[1  1  0]
